subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which sub-environments and sedimentary structures characterize the tidal flat depositional environment?
options: Intertidal mudflats dominated by desiccation cracks, evaporite crusts and wind-blown silt, showing a complete absence of marine indicators
Supratidal marsh deposits consisting of laminated organic-rich mud with root traces, gypsum crusts and pyrite framboids, formed exclusively above the high tide line
Subtidal channel sands showing unimodal cross-bedding, gravel lags and a complete absence of mud drapes or bipolar current indicators
Supratidal (marsh), intertidal (mudflat, sandflat), subtidal (channel). Herringbone cross-bedding, flaser bedding, lenticular bedding
solution: Tidal: bipolar cross-bedding (ebb + flood). Mud drapes. Reactivation surfaces.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Pencil cleavage, which yields slender pencil-shaped rock fragments in deformed rocks, develops under which condition?
options: Two cleavages intersect at high angle
A single cleavage overprints undeformed strata
Primary bedding is preserved without any strain
Shear stress rotates pre-existing fold hinges
solution: Pencil cleavage: intersection of two cleavages at ~90°. Rock breaks into pencil-shaped fragments. Common in fold hinges.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the primary purpose of core drilling, and which bit is typically used?
options: Bores only through soil using a rotating hollow-stem auger flight system
Crushes rock by repeated impacts of a heavy falling cutting tool
Uses a percussive chisel with no recovery of a continuous sample
Obtains intact rock core. Diamond bit. Core barrel. HQ, NQ, BQ sizes
solution: Core sizes: HQ (63.5mm), NQ (47.6mm), BQ (36.5mm). Recovery ratio: % core recovered.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Stretching lineation, the long axis of deformed grains or objects, is oriented parallel to which strain axis?
options: Long axis of deformed objects/grains. Parallel to X-strain axis. In L-tectonites (rodding)
Z-axis direction of the finite strain ellipsoid, perpendicular to the direction of maximum elongation
Y-axis direction of the finite strain ellipsoid, the intermediate principal axis
X-axis direction of the finite strain ellipsoid, parallel to maximum shortening
solution: L-tectonite: rod-like fabric. L-S tectonite: planar + linear. S-tectonite: planar only.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Landforms produced by rivers, glaciers, wind, waves, groundwater and volcanoes are grouped under which classification scheme?
options: Landforms are classified into only two categories: fluvial and glacial
Landforms are produced exclusively by river and wind erosion processes
Landforms are classified by their overall size rather than the process that formed them
Fluvial (river), Glacial, Aeolian (wind), Coastal, Karst, Volcanic
solution: Geomorphology: study of landforms and processes. Dynamic equilibrium.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In komatiite flows, spinifex olivine blades and a B-zone of random olivine result from differentiation, and these lavas erupted at about:
options: Andesite flow dominated by plagioclase and pyroxene phenocrysts with blocky aa lava surfaces and thick flows
Spinifex (olivine blades) + B-zone (random olivine). Thermal erosion channels. ~1600°C eruption T
Basalt flow forming pillow structures, columnar joints and extensive flood plateau basalts
Rhyolite flow with prominent flow banding and large quartz and sanidine phenocrysts
solution: Komatiite: Archean. High MgO (>18%). Channelized flow. Ni-sulfide deposits (Kambalda).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Aquifer parameter estimation: type curve matching:
options: Measure transmissivity directly from the static water level before pumping begins
Compute both T and S from the well's depth and its casing diameter alone
Match observed drawdown curve to Theis type curve. Read T and S from match point
Estimate T and S from regional rainfall and geology without a pumping test
solution: Theis type curve: W(u) vs 1/u. Match point gives T and S. Automated now (parameter estimation).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In Miller indices, the notation (hkl) is obtained from what property of crystal faces?
options: Plane angles. (111), (100) and (110) record the interfacial angles between crystal faces
Interaxial angles. The triplets (111), (100) and (110) describe the angular setting of the crystallographic axes
Intercepts on crystal axes. (111): octahedron. (100): cube. (110): dodecahedron. Negative: bar over index
Directions. (111), (100) and (110) give the linear growth direction of crystal edges
solution: Miller: reciprocal of intercepts. Zero = parallel to axis. Dhkl = a/√(h²+k²+l²) (cubic).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Shear zone vs fault: shear zones are ductile deformation at depth, faults are brittle at shallow levels. Transition occurs at:
options: The Mohorovičić discontinuity, below which deformation becomes purely brittle and rigid
A fixed depth of exactly 5 km that is independent of the local geothermal gradient
The depth of the brittle-ductile transition, which lies near 100 km beneath ocean crust
Brittle-ductile transition (~10-15km in continental crust)
solution: BDT: quartz: ~300°C, feldspar: ~450°C. Depth depends on geothermal gradient.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The boundary separating the crust from the mantle is the:
options: Mohorovičić discontinuity (Moho)
Gutenberg discontinuity, marked by a sharp jump in P-wave velocity
Conrad surface, defined by a sudden acceleration of S-waves at depth
Lehmann discontinuity, where P-wave velocity rises abruptly beneath the crust
solution: The Moho marks the crust–mantle boundary, identified by a jump in seismic velocity.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Crystal system with 6-fold symmetry axis is:
options: Hexagonal
Cubic
Tetragonal
Orthorhombic
solution: Hexagonal: one 6-fold axis.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In paleoclimate studies, δ¹⁸O measured in marine foraminifera tests serves as a proxy for what?
options: Paleoclimate proxy. Marine δ¹⁸O → ice volume + T. Foraminifera tests. G. bulloides, G. ruber
Carbon isotope ratios measured in marine organic matter and carbonate shell tests
Sulfur isotope ratios of sulfide minerals preserved in the sedimentary rock record
Nitrogen isotope ratios of organic sediments and interstitial pore waters of sedimentary basins, marine and coastal
solution: δ¹⁸O: warmer = lighter (more ¹⁶O incorporated). Marine isotope stages (MIS). VSMOW, PDB standards.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes landfill leachate and the chemical constituents it carries?
options: Dissolved organic and inorganic contaminants
Only suspended plastic debris and macro-scale litter
Only clean groundwater free of any dissolved metals
Only airborne dust particles carried by surface winds
solution: Leachate: water percolating through waste picks up contaminants. Requires liner and collection system. Contaminates groundwater.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: At a station the S-wave arrives 15 s after the P-wave. Using ~8 km per second of S–P delay, the epicentral distance is about:
options: 120 km
60 km
15 km
240 km
solution: distance ≈ (S−P time) × 8 km/s = 15×8 = 120 km.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The bioturbation index of a sedimentary rock measures the degree of what activity?
options: Degree of biogenic reworking
Average grain size of the deposit
Paleo-water temperature of the basin
Strength of carbonate cementation
solution: BI: 0-6 scale. 0 = no bioturbation, 6 = complete homogenization. Reflects oxygenation, sedimentation rate.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In carbonate rocks, which types of porosity are recognized, and which type tends to dominate?
options: Primary interparticle porosity preserved between well-rounded grains, with no evidence of secondary dissolution at all
Only vuggy porosity formed by dissolution of evaporite nodules, with no interparticle or moldic pore types present
Interparticle, intraparticle, moldic, vuggy, fenestral, fracture, channel. Secondary porosity dominant
Only fracture porosity developed along tectonic joints, with all interparticle and moldic pores completely occluded
solution: Carbonates: primary porosity low after diagenesis. Secondary: dissolution (moldic, vuggy). Choquette-Pray classification.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Grooves and scratches on a polished fault surface, known as slickenside striations, help geologists determine what?
options: Direction of fault movement
Orientation of the regional fold hinge line
Direction of paleocurrent in the host sediment
Attitude of the original depositional bedding
solution: Slickensides: polished/striated fault surface. Striations parallel to movement direction. Riedel shears indicate sense.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which classification diagram, Total Alkali vs Silica, is used for volcanic rocks?
options: Silica plotted against alumina to separate peraluminous from metaluminous suites
Iron/magnesium ratio against alkali content to subdivide tholeiitic series
Potassium versus sodium diagram used to name plutonic rocks of the QAPF system
Total Alkali vs Silica. Le Maitre et al. Classification of volcanic rocks
solution: TAS: 15 fields. Basalt, andesite, dacite, rhyolite, trachyte, phonolite. Alkaline vs subalkaline.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: During partial melting of pelitic rocks, which reaction produces migmatite melt?
options: Eutectic melting of a dry basaltic protolith producing a quartz-undersaturated melt without any residual solid phase
Congruent melting of a pure albite composition at the vapor-saturated solidus leaving a melt of identical composition
Muscovite + quartz + plagioclase + H₂O → melt (migmatite). Biotite dehydration melting at higher T
Dry melting of mantle peridotite at pressures above the anhydrous solidus producing a refractory harzburgite residue
solution: Pelite: fluid-present (Ms breakdown) → fluid-absent (Bt dehydration). P-T of solidus varies.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In GIS, which analysis determines the areas visible from one or more observation points using line-of-sight between cells?
options: A region within a fixed circular radius, independent of terrain elevation changes
The area that drains to a common outlet, computed from the flow accumulation
A zone of equal slope gradient, derived from the digital elevation model
Area visible from point(s). Line-of-sight. For towers, observation points
solution: Viewshed: cumulative visibility. Observer height + target height. Multiple observers.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a braided river facies model, the deposits are characterized by what pattern of channels and bar forms?
options: Delta with a single channel and extensive muddy prodelta deposits
Sheet-like, multiple channels. Bar forms (longitudinal, transverse, diagonal). Vertically stacked, pebbly
Meandering single channel with lateral accretion surfaces and abundant fine-grained overbank mud deposits
Tidal estuary with bidirectional current structures and mud drapes
solution: Braided: flashy discharge. Gravel sheets. No fine-grained overbank. Non-cyclic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral specimen of mass 78 g has a volume of 30 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
solution: SG = mass/volume = 78/30 = 2.6.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Sandstone is best described as which type of rock composed of sand-sized grains?
options: Clastic sedimentary rock made of sand-sized grains
Foliated metamorphic rock produced by regional metamorphism of shale
Chemical limestone formed by precipitation from warm shallow seawater
Intrusive igneous rock that cooled slowly deep beneath the surface
solution: Sandstone is a clastic rock of cemented sand (mostly quartz) grains.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Seismic reflection survey: Common Midpoint (CMP) gathering improves:
options: Signal-to-noise ratio through stacking
Lateral resolution of the migrated section
The frequency content of the recorded wavelet
The vertical resolution of the stacked traces
solution: CMP: multiple traces share same midpoint. Stack after NMO correction. Improves S/N by sqrt(n) where n = fold.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Image classification: supervised vs unsupervised:
options: Supervised: clustering (unknown classes). Unsupervised: training sites (known classes)
Both approaches rely on the analyst's field knowledge before classification
Supervised: no training. Unsupervised: user-defined training polygons
Supervised: training sites (known classes). Unsupervised: clustering (unknown classes)
solution: Supervised: ML, Maximum Likelihood, SVM. Unsupervised: K-means, ISODATA.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which statement about coalification is correct?
options: It converts coal into limestone and carbonate rocks during deep burial
It reduces the carbon content while raising the moisture percentage
It increases fixed carbon and reduces volatile matter
It increases the moisture content and lowers the heating value of the coal
solution: Progressive burial heat raises rank: more fixed carbon, less moisture and volatiles.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ophiolite emplacement: how does oceanic crust get on top of continental?
options: Emplacement by strike-slip faulting during ridge transgression
Subduction of the continental slab beneath the oceanic crust
Growth of new oceanic crust in situ at a mid-ocean ridge
Obduction during continental collision (rare)
solution: Obduction: oceanic crust thrust onto continent. Oman ophiolite. SSZ (supra-subduction zone) type.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ore microscopy: reflected light identification:
options: Identification by reflected colour alone, because all sulfide minerals appear identical in polished section under the ore microscope
Distinction based purely on crystal habit and internal grain boundary relationships
Determination restricted to wet-chemical spot tests on crushed ore powder
Pyrite: high reflectance, yellow, hard. Chalcopyrite: brass yellow, soft. Galena: bright white, cubic
solution: Ore microscopy: polished section. Reflectance, color, hardness (streak), bireflectance, anisotropy.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following are the principal Archean cratons recognised within the Indian shield?
options: Dharwar (W & E), Singhbhum, Bastar, Bundelkhand, Rajasthan (Aravalli)
Dharwar and the Deccan Traps, together with the Kutch sedimentary cover
Singhbhum and the Vindhyan basin, with the Cuddapah platform cover
Bundelkhand and the Siwalik molasse belt of the Himalayan foothills
solution: Dharwar Craton: 3.4-2.5 Ga. Divided by Closepet Granite into E and W Dharwar.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Shield volcanoes, stratovolcanoes, cinder cones, calderas and lava domes are landforms produced by which geological agent?
options: Shield volcano (basalt), stratovolcano (andesite), cinder cone, caldera, lava dome
All volcanic landforms are constructed entirely from repeated basaltic lava flows
All volcanic landforms are steep-sided cones built exclusively from explosive ash and pyroclastic eruptions
All volcanic landforms are broad, low-angled plateaus formed by repeated effusive eruptions
solution: Shield: Hawaii (gentle slopes). Stratovolcano: Fuji, Vesuvius (steep, explosive). Caldera: Crater Lake.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Compared with surface (opencast) mining, underground coal mining is generally chosen when the seam is:
options: Deep, so that the stripping ratio becomes uneconomic
Shallow, so that stripping the overburden is cheap and easy
Always, regardless of seam depth or stripping ratio
Very shallow and thick so that opencast extraction is impractical
solution: When overburden-to-coal (stripping) ratio is too high for opencast, underground methods become economic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which pairing of fault type and stress is correct?
options: Reverse fault — no stress
Normal fault — compressional stress
Normal fault — tensional stress
Reverse fault — tensional stress
solution: Tension produces normal faults; compression produces reverse/thrust faults.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: At the 410 km and 660 km discontinuities in the mantle transition zone, what mineral phase changes occur?
options: Temperature changes. Sharp thermal jumps mark both boundaries but no mineral change
Olivine → wadsleyite (410 km) and ringwoodite → perovskite + magnesiowüstite (660 km). Phase changes
Melting. Partial fusion generates the seismic velocity reductions observed at both depths
Compositional changes. A wholesale change in bulk chemistry separates the upper mantle from the lower mantle at depth
solution: Transition zone: seismic velocity jumps. Topography on 410 and 660 = mantle T anomalies.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Stromatolites: layered sedimentary structures formed by:
options: Fungi mats that bind carbonate sediment in deep marine basins
Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae). Precambrian to Recent
Vascular plant roots that stabilise sediment on exposed tidal flats
Chemosynthetic bacteria limited to hydrothermal vent environments
solution: Stromatolite: laminated, domical. Cyanobacteria trap/bind sediment. Shark Bay (Australia).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ammonites are excellent Mesozoic index fossils due to rapid evolution and wide distribution; their suture lines range from ceratitic to:
options: Paleozoic index fossils. Slow evolution, narrow distribution, confined to shallow shelf seas
Mesozoic index fossils. Rapid evolution, wide distribution. Ceratitic vs ammonitic suture lines
Index fossils throughout all eras, with suture lines that remain simple and entirely unchanged since the Cambrian
Cenozoic index fossils with straight, uncoiled shells restricted to deep ocean basins
solution: Ammonites: Mollusca, Cephalopoda. Suture: goniatitic → ceratitic → ammonitic (increasing complexity).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Paleoenvironmental indicators: evaporites indicate:
options: Deep oceanic basins below the carbonate compensation depth with vigorous upwelling
Humid continental settings where rainfall exceeds evaporation throughout the year
Wet climate with abundant rainfall and a positive freshwater budget
Arid, restricted basin. High evaporation, limited inflow
solution: Evaporite: sabkha, restricted lagoon, saline lake. Arid climate indicator.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Radiolaria: siliceous microfossils. Used for:
options: Deep marine biostratigraphy, paleoceanography
Terrestrial soil correlation using wind-blown silica grains
Shallow marine reef correlation using carbonate test dissolution rates
Freshwater lake zonation based on calcareous resting cysts alone
solution: Radiolaria: SiO2 tests. Deep sea sediments. Biostratigraphic zonation for Mesozoic-Cenozoic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which unconformity is characterized by older folded or tilted strata overlain by horizontal strata?
options: Parallel strata with a long time gap that is recognized only from fossils
Older folded strata overlain by horizontal strata
Sedimentary strata resting directly on eroded crystalline igneous basement rock
Steeply dipping igneous intrusions truncated by a flat-lying sedimentary cover sequence
solution: Angular: represents orogeny + erosion + renewed deposition. Great Unconformity (Grand Canyon).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The section shows 40 m of overburden above a 3 m coal seam. The volumetric stripping ratio (overburden : coal thickness) is:
solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 40/3 = 13.33 : 1.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The upper surface of the zone of saturation in the ground is the:
options: Bedrock surface
Soil horizon A
Capillary fringe top
Water table
solution: The water table marks the top of the saturated zone, below which pores are water-filled.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To which structural class of silicates does the common mineral quartz belong?
options: Phyllosilicates (sheet silicates with water)
Cyclosilicates (ring silicate structures)
Nesosilicates (independent tetrahedra only)
Tectosilicates (framework silicates)
solution: Quartz: SiO2 framework. No cleavage. Conchoidal fracture. Piezoelectric.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which fossil group, characterised by a spiral-coiled chambered shell, underwent rapid evolution and became extinct at the end of the Cretaceous?
options: Trilobites
Ammonites
Graptolites
Fusulinids
solution: Ammonites: shelled cephalopods with rapid evolution and wide distribution; excellent Mesozoic index fossils (ammonite biozones). Extinct at the K-Pg boundary.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: GPS (Global Positioning System): minimum 4 satellites for:
options: 3D position (x,y,z) without any receiver clock correction
3D position (x,y,z) and receiver clock bias
2D position and elevation estimated from the same signals
Precise time only, position is determined by a single satellite
solution: 4 satellites: solve for 4 unknowns (x,y,z,dt). More satellites improve geometry (DOP).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How does continued sediment deposition affect a reservoir, and which storage zones does it reduce?
options: Deposition of silt in a reservoir always increases the useful storage capacity
Sediment deposition reduces storage capacity. Dead storage + live storage
Fine sediment settles only at the dam face and never near the inlet
Erosion of the catchment adds clean water that improves the storage
solution: Sedimentation: rate depends on catchment erosion. Flushing, sluicing. Check dams in tributaries.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What igneous texture is characterized by gas cavities (vesicles) in a volcanic rock?
options: Shear fabric produced by ductile deformation during regional metamorphism
Fabric developed by welding of glass shards in hot pyroclastic deposits
Gas cavities (vesicles) in volcanic rock
Cavities later filled with secondary minerals such as quartz and calcite
solution: Vesicles: gas bubbles trapped in lava. Amygdules: filled vesicles.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Biostratigraphic zone: range zone defined by:
options: The most abundant fossil species in a local measured column
A dated volcanic ash bed that caps the local succession
The last appearance of a fossil genus in a measured section
First and last appearance of index fossil
solution: Range zone: FAD to LAD of index fossil. Assemblage zone: characteristic assemblage.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Under what conditions does hummocky cross-stratification (HCS) typically form in marine sediments?
options: Formed by tidal currents in a shallow estuary. Bipolar foresets with mud drapes
Formed by storm waves below fair-weather wave base. Undulating sets, low angle
Formed by oscillatory waves above fair-weather wave base in a high-energy foreshore
Formed by unidirectional turbidity currents on the continental slope. Sole marks present
solution: HCS: diagnostic of storm-dominated shelves. Hummocks: 3D cross-sets. Swales: concave down.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A clockwise P-T path, typical of collisional orogens, records which sequence of events?
options: Burial→heating→exhumation. Typical for collisional orogens. Andalusite→kyanite→sillimanite
Heating→burial→exhumation. Typical of extensional rift settings. Cordierite→sillimanite
Constant pressure with rising temperature. Typical of contact metamorphism around shallow plutons
Rapid burial without heating, followed by isothermal decompression and final exhumation
solution: Clockwise: Barrovian. ITD (isothermal decompression). Counterclockwise: high T/low P (Buchan).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In well logging, the gamma ray tool detects natural radiation from which elements, and what does a high API reading indicate?
options: Measures induced radioactivity from a neutron source to estimate the formation porosity directly
Natural γ (K, U, Th). Shale indicator (high API). Clean sand: low GR. Spectral GR: Th/U ratio for redox
Records the acoustic travel time of compressional waves to derive matrix and fluid volume
Maps formation resistivity by focussing the survey current into the bed with a guarded electrode sonde array
solution: GR: permeable zones (low GR). Shale volume: V_sh = (GR - GR_clean)/(GR_shale - GR_clean).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An ore body of 2 Mt has an average metal grade of 3%. The contained metal is about:
options: 60 kt
30 kt
6 kt
120 kt
solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 2 Mt × 3% = 60 thousand tonnes (kt).
